articles.summary: Kering shares soared on Wednesday after the French luxury group’s second-quarter results indicated its turnaround plan is gaining traction. The better-than-expected performance of its star brand Gucci cheered investors, prompting a flurry of upgrades from analysts. Kering shares rose 16.9 percent to close at 292.85 euros, leading a mixed performance by luxury stocks.

articles.headline: The Black Beauty Roster Beauty Show Brings Out The Biggest Names In Beauty
articles.author: Keyaira Boone
articles.summary: The Black Beauty Roster Beauty Show brought out the biggest names in beauty Monday. Danessa Myricks, Derek J, Jesseca Dupart, Sabrina Dhowre Elba and more hit the event ready to celebrate the power of inclusive beauty. The trade event brought founders, stylists, makeup artists, and creators to New York’s Chelsea Industrial venue. It included demonstrations from expert beauty professionals, master classes, product testing opportunities, and panels. There was even a traditional beauty hair battle where stylists competed for a cash prize. Susy Oludele, who created the breathtaking finale look for Sammy B’s 2023 runway show, served as one of the judges.

articles.headline: People Are Willing To Go Into Debt For Beauty Products, Report Shows
articles.author: Daniel Miller
articles.summary: Personal care is essential for many nationwide and some are willing to sacrifice a little more financially at retail stores to ensure they secure their critical beauty supplies. Whether it's hair products or skin care items, a recent survey sheds light on what people are spending cash on for self-care maintenance. Zenoti, a software platform designed for the beauty, wellness, and fitness industries, conducted a survey of 1,000 adults in the United States to inquire about their beauty and wellness spending and what they sacrifice to purchase these goods.

articles.headline: Chanel And Lincoln Center Celebrate The BAAND Together Dance Festival
articles.author: Jenna Adrian-Diaz
articles.summary: A night spent watching any of the five renowned New York City-based dance companies—Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, American Ballet Theater, Ballet Hispánico, Dance Theater of Harlem, and New York City Ballet—is a treat. But the chance to see all five in a single night is almost unheard of. Alas, Lincoln Center’s BAAND Together Dance Festival transforms that rêve into reality. Now in its sixth year thanks to the longstanding support of Chanel, the festival was ushered in by an opening night celebration filled with cocktails and small bites at Lincoln Center’s own culinary hot ticket, chef Kwame Onwuachi’s Afro-Caribbean restaurant Tatiana.

articles.headline: Puig Reports First-Half Revenue Growth After Estee Lauder Talks End
articles.author: Mireia Merino and Marta Serafinko
articles.summary: Spanish beauty company Puig's (PUIGb.MC), opens new tab first-half revenue grew 4.4% like-for-like basis, it said on ‌Thursday as it posted its first results since talks ended in May on a possible merger with U.S. cosmetics company Estée Lauder. The collapse of the talks has shifted investor focus back to Puig's standalone growth prospects as fragrance demand normalises following a post-pandemic ⁠boom in feel-good products, and as conflict in the Middle East weighs on travel retail, an important channel for premium beauty brands.

articles.headline: Derma Beauty And Hair Care Power L’Oréal To Record Half-Year Operating Margin
articles.summary: L’Oréal has published its 2026 half-year results, where hair care was revealed as a front-runner and its two most clinically oriented divisions Professional Products and DermatoloBetween 2022 and 2025, Gucci lost over €4.5 billion in revenue, falling below the €6 billion mark last year. The Florentine house is nevertheless still the Kering group’s flagship label. And is still in the spotlight, now that Kering’s CEO Luca De Meo, appointed in September 2025, is implementing the ‘ReconKering’ action plan, whose primary aim is to revitalise the house led by Francesca Bellettini. At the end of H1 2026, Gucci’s turnaround still seems a tough proposition, but the group owned by the Pinault family appears to have set the house on the right track, despite results that are still weak.

articles.headline: Estée Lauder Taps Hailee Steinfeld For Glimmer Fragrance Launch
articles.author: Gisselle Gaitan
articles.summary: To launch its new Glimmer fragrance, Estée Lauder is unveiling a campaign that taps into the fragrance's ethos and stars actress and singer Hailee Steinfeld. An amber floral scent, Glimmer will be rolling out with an initiative that showcases how its fragrance can inspire optimism and leave a lasting impression, the brand shared. “Fragrance has an incredible ability to tell a story without words, evoke emotion, and create memories that stay with you,” said Steinfeld. “What drew me to Glimmer is that it's more than a fragrance; it's a feeling and I’m honored to be a part of it.”

articles.headline: Gucci Seemingly On Cusp Of Turnaround
articles.author: Olivier Guyot
articles.summary: Between 2022 and 2025, Gucci lost over €4.5 billion in revenue, falling below the €6 billion mark last year. The Florentine house is nevertheless still the Kering group’s flagship label. And is still in the spotlight, now that Kering’s CEO Luca De Meo, appointed in September 2025, is implementing the ‘ReconKering’ action plan, whose primary aim is to revitalise the house led by Francesca Bellettini. At the end of H1 2026, Gucci’s turnaround still seems a tough proposition, but the group owned by the Pinault family appears to have set the house on the right track, despite results that are still weak.

articles.headline: L'Oreal To Launch First Gucci Beauty Products As Early As 2028, CEO Says
articles.author: Inti Landauro
articles.summary: L'Oreal plans to launch its first Gucci ‌beauty products as early as 2028, the company's Chief Executive Nicolas Hieronimus said on ⁠Thursday, adding he was "super ambitious" for the brand that is also showing signs of improvement in its core fashion and leather goods ‌lines. L'Oreal ⁠is set to take over the licence to produce beauty products ⁠for the Gucci brand from Coty in mid 2027 as ⁠part of a €4 billion deal signed ⁠with Kering late last year.

articles.headline: L’Oréal Introduces Beauty's Biggest Stage Yet
articles.author: Billie Rose Scholz
articles.summary: L’Oréal is moving beauty from backstage to center stage with its exclusive two-year contract with Plenitude Arena, Europe’s largest indoor venue in Nanterre, France. The arena sees over 2 million visitors annually through its significant cultural and sporting events, including Celine Dion’s residency, and concerts by Olivia Rodrigo, Muse, and more, as well as the Rolex Paris Masters. The partnership provides L’Oréal with visibility through digital screens, immersive beauty activations, and pop-up spaces, and serves as a hospitality platform, allowing L’Oréal to invite its employees and business partners to enjoy major musical and sporting events. This announcement also highlights the local connection between the organizations, as L’Oréal’s global headquarters is located in Clichy, near Nanterre.

articles.headline: L’Oréal’s Secret Sauce For Growth
articles.author: Jennifer Weil
articles.summary: L’Oréal’s business — and that of the beauty market — keep picking up speed. The company’s second-quarter revenues broadly beat market expectations, registering 6.3 percent adjusted like-for-like growth to 11.62 billion euros. That compares to consensus of 5.6 percent. The market smiled on L’Oréal’s results a day after their release. Its stock closed Thursday up 2.7 percent to 394 euros.

articles.headline: L’Oréal CEO Nicolas Hieronimus Bets On A.I. to Extend A Nearly $100B Family Fortune
articles.author: Beth Duckett
articles.summary: More than a century after chemist Eugène Schueller turned a hair-dye formula into the business that became L’Oréal, the beauty giant is still finding new ways to grow, with A.I. as its latest bet. L’Oréal’s Revenue rose 6.3 percent on a like-for-like basis, a key retail metric, to €11.6 billion ($13.2 billion) in the April-June quarter. For the first half of 2026, revenue increased 5.8 percent to €23.78 billion ($27.1 billion), while net profit climbed 4.7 percent to €3.96 billion ($4.5 billion) and the operating margin reached 21.3 percent. Growth extended across every region and division, from Maybelline’s mass-market makeup to La Roche-Posay’s dermatological skincare and Kérastase’s salon-grade haircare.

articles.headline: From A Growth Market To A Global Capability Hub: China’s Evolving Role In Beauty
articles.summary: China’s beauty market is going through another period of change — beyond being the world’s largest beauty market, it’s one of the most demanding. According to McKinsey, while the Chinese beauty market grew by 3 percent in 2023, the category is projected to maintain 6 percent compound annual growth rate from 2024 until 2028. A 2025 McKinsey survey expects a lower volume growth due to inflation and cautious consumer spending, but 75 percent of beauty executives said they’re doubling down on sales growth.

articles.headline: It's Official: This Is The Number-One Chanel Bag Of 2026
articles.author: Anna Laplaca
articles.summary: When the first Chanel collection designed by Matthieu Blazy hit stores in March, it caused a frenzy of fashion-people purchases. Some of the hottest-ticket items included the two-tone pumps and the pony-hair ballet flats, but the handbags were another story entirely. The reimagined 2.55 Handbag had people buzzing after its runway debut and the Large Tote also garnered attention for its celebrity stamps of approval by Hailey Bieber, Kylie Jenner, and Blackpink’s Jennie. Despite this, the one Chanel bag that everyone in fashion actually bought and wore from Blazy's spring/summer 2026 debut is the Small Shopping Bag.

articles.headline: Formula 1: Flavio Briatore On Alpine’s Rise & Gucci Partnership
articles.summary: Flavio Briatore, Alpine's executive advisor, discusses the team's impressive growth from an $80 million valuation to $3.5 billion during his recent interview on The Race. He highlights key strategies, such as securing Gucci as a title sponsor, transforming the team's culture, and focusing on performance improvement. Additionally, Briatore emphasizes the need for more sprint races and the successful execution of a marketing revolution from his Benetton days. His optimistic outlook reflects a belief that Alpine can reclaim its competitive edge in Formula 1.

articles.headline: Gucci's Highly Anticipated La Famiglia Collection Has Finally Hit Stores
articles.author: Caroline Cubbin
articles.summary: After the La Famiglia campaign was released last September, it wasn't long before the collection—Demna's first for the label, ahead of his debut runway presentation in February—became an instant obsession for celebrities, editors, and fashion fans alike. With its buzzy, narrative-driven campaign, comprised of a memorable cast of character archetypes defined by unique styles, and accompanying film, The Tiger, it became clear that the daring, classically sophisticated look cultivated in each and every handbag, shoe, jewelry piece, and ready-to-wear item would soon be a fixture of the label under Demna's visionary creative direction.

articles.headline: How Unilever Is Transforming Brand Building With Creators, Social Media And AI
articles.author: Molly Innes
articles.summary: A changing consumer environment has necessitated a marketing transformation, is the view of Unilever, one of the biggest consumer goods organisations in the world. That transformation has seen it exponentially increase the number of creators it works with and commit to a “social-first” approach, something that has attracted a lot of attention. In this episode of The Marketing Week Podcast, news editor Niamh Carroll is joined by Unilever’s beauty and wellbeing division global vice president of digital, social and AI transformation Selina Sykes.

articles.headline: Beauty & Personal Care Brands Lean Into Summerween
articles.author: Lianna Albrizio
articles.summary: Consumers are howling for spooky season, and beauty and personal care brands are capitalizing on this Summerween trend – a mid-summer “holiday” where celebrants start getting into the Halloween spirit as early as July and August. A newcomer in the Summerween hype is Lush Cosmetics. “Lush loves life, and we’ll take any reason to celebrate!” Erica Vegan, Lush Cosmetics product expert, told Happi. “There are plenty of us Lushies who are absolute fanatics about Halloween, and when it gets hot and sticky outside, we start yearning for our cauldrons and cooler weather. It seems more and more people are feeling the same way, which is exactly why Summerween has become such a fun celebration. This is actually our first summer celebrating Summerween this early, and we couldn’t be more delighted. Summerween is all about bringing the magic, nostalgia, and playful spirit of Halloween into the middle of summer, proving there’s never a wrong time to celebrate your favorite season.”

articles.headline: Retail’s New Operating Model Centers On Leaner Teams, Smarter Data And Physical Community
articles.author: Zofia Zwieglinska
articles.summary: At a recent Brand Leaders Dinner hosted by Glossy and Modern Retail, in partnership with Global Payments, founders and C-suite executives from across fashion, beauty and retail gathered to discuss the pressures shaping their businesses, from artificial intelligence and changing hiring plans to the rising cost of building awareness at retail. The discussion was held under Chatham House Rules, allowing attendees to speak candidly without their comments being attributed to them or their companies.

articles.headline: Shein’s New Brand Accelerator Is Fueling Growth For Emerging And Established U.S. Brands
articles.summary: One of the biggest challenges fashion brands face today is unreliable supply chains and inventory management to accurately meet customer demand and expectations. These barriers are especially intimidating when brands are looking to expand internationally — operational missteps can often lead to growth stagnation. To help brands overcome this recurring challenge, Shein launched its Xcelerator program in September 2025. The program was initially launched in France and the U.K. — and now is expanding to the U.S. for brands looking to take the next step in their growth journey.

articles.headline: Choosing Cruelty-Free Cosmetics: Activism Through Alternatives
articles.author: Faith Sweazy
articles.summary: Anyone who’s been active on Instagram lately has likely been emotionally struck by the story of the Ridglan Farms beagles that were recently liberated by animal welfare activists and major animal welfare organizations in Dane County, Wisconsin. If you haven’t, let me fill you in: The Ridglan Farms Biomedical Research Facility in Blue Mounds, Wisconsin was raided twice by animal rights activists this past March and April, with 23 beagles being freed in the process. The facility, which breeds thousands of dogs, has over 300 code violations and struck a deal in 2025 to discontinue its beagle breeding operations by July of 2026. More recently, Ridglan Farm’s attorney has created an agreement with Big Dog Ranch Rescue to transfer the remaining dogs in their facility.

articles.headline: Balm Foundations Are Beauty’s Next Big Thing – And Midlife Women Love L'Oréal Paris’ Entry To The Category
articles.author: Josie O’Brien
articles.summary: Liquid, powder, cream, mousse and stick – these are the foundation types you’ve probably tried at one point or another. But one texture that’s having a resurgence in the era of less-is-more beauty is balm. Balm foundations first rose to prominence in the Nineties amid a focus on natural-looking complexions and skin-friendly textures. Their popularity faded in the 2010s, when full-coverage, ultra-matte makeup dominated the beauty landscape.

articles.headline: July In Review: L’Oréal Lands Gucci Beauty, US FDA Peptide Decision, EU Fragrance Allergen Deadline
articles.author: Sabine Waldeck
articles.summary: Last month, in personal care industry news, L’Oréal announced plans to take over the 50-year exclusive global license agreement for Gucci Beauty, a year ahead of schedule. Asia’s beauty market advanced. Companies across the region ramped up AI investments, and on the finance side, a US investment firm filed for the first dedicated K-beauty ETF (exchange-traded fund). Meanwhile, the US FDA’s Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee assessed whether seven injectable peptides should be used in compounded medicines.

articles.headline: China Insight: How AI Is Redefining Fashion, Beauty And The Future Of Consumer Innovation
articles.author: Li Jun
articles.summary: The 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference here marked a defining moment for China’s AI ecosystem: artificial intelligence has moved beyond experimentation and entered a new phase of commercial deployment. The scale of this year’s event reflected that transformation. Exhibition space surpassed 1 million square feet for the first time, with more than 1,100 companies showcasing 3,000-plus technological achievements and more than 300 global first releases. Offline attendance exceeded 300,000 visitors, while 57 key application scenarios secured 16.2 billion yuan, or $23.7 million, in intended cooperation ahead of the conference.

articles.headline: AI‑Generated Fashion Models: Innovation, Illusion Or A Step Too Far?
articles.summary: Fashion has always sold aspiration. Long before artificial intelligence (AI), it relied on carefully constructed images of beauty through styling, lighting, makeup and, more recently, digital retouching. While consumers may have understood that these images do not reflect everyday reality, they continued to engage with them. They followed fashion trends and they bought the products being advertised.

articles.headline: The Hair Care Brands That Dominate AI Search
articles.author: Noor Lobad
articles.summary: Hair care is a highly concentrated category when it comes to AI visibility, new data shows. An analysis of the results of 300 hair care-specific prompts and fan-out queries run through ChatGPT by digital agency Avenue Z in June showed that the top five brands accounted for 49 percent of total hair care visibility.

articles.headline: Fashion’s Circular Ambitions Face a Legal Ceiling
articles.author: Kimiya Shams
articles.summary: French courts have handed luxury giants back-to-back wins against upcycling designers, reinforcing a simple principle: consumers may resell branded goods, but they may not reconstruct them into new commercial products. As fashion’s waste crisis deepens, those decisions expose a growing tension between circularity and intellectual property rights. The practice of transforming existing products and materials into new creations – commonly known as “upcycling” – has gained significant traction across the fashion industry in recent years. Patagonia repurposes retired rain jackets into compact travel cases. H&M Beyond has partnered with Revibe on a limited-edition upcycled collection. Luxury houses have also embraced the practice: Gucci’s Equilibrium program reclaims surplus production materials, Hermès repurposes remnants from past collections, and Salvatore Ferragamo gives vintage silk new life in footwear and leather goods.

articles.headline: Have You Heard Of Biotech Beauty? We Took A Closer Look
articles.author: Kati Chitrakorn
articles.summary: Mihwa Kim loved makeup so much that she became a host on a beauty home shopping show in South Korea — comparing, testing and promoting dozens of products on television. Then in 2013, her career was upended when a devastating car accident left severe wounds on her face and neck requiring more than 60 stitches. Her confidence took a huge hit. For six months she shut herself away at home and avoided sunlight as much as possible while she attempted to recover both physically and emotionally.

articles.headline: National Lipstick Day: The Packaging Behind One Of Beauty’s Most Iconic Products
articles.summary: Every year on July 29, beauty enthusiasts celebrate National Lipstick Day—a tribute to one of the most recognizable and enduring products in the cosmetics industry. From classic reds to modern nude palettes, lipstick has long been a symbol of self-expression, confidence, and personal style. While trends, shades, and formulations continue to evolve, one thing remains constant: packaging plays a critical role in how consumers experience and perceive a lipstick product. For beauty brands, lipstick packaging is often far more than a container. It is an extension of the brand itself.

articles.headline: Chanel Retains Top Spot, Massimo Dutti, Celine And Phoebe Philo Surge On Lyst’s Hottest Brands Ranking
articles.author: Tianwei Zhang
articles.summary: Chanel has retained its position as the world’s hottest brand in the latest Lyst Index for the second quarter of 2026, reflecting how the platform’s updated methodology continues to reward sustained cultural momentum rather than one‑off viral spikes.

articles.headline: Chanel Sales Jump 16% As New Collections Boost Label’s Appeal
articles.author: Angelina Rascouet
articles.summary: Chanel’s sales rose by double digits in the first half, beating luxury rivals including LVMH, as wealthy shoppers splurged on the new fashion creations of designer Matthieu Blazy. Comparable revenue climbed by about 16% at Chanel Ltd. in the period, a person familiar with the performance said, declining to be identified because the figures haven’t been made public. Sales at the fashion division — the largest unit — grew by a similar percentage, the person said.

articles.headline: Too Faced Co-Founder Reveals True Thoughts On Impact Of Estée Lauder Companies Acquisition
articles.author: Lynsey Barber
articles.summary: Speaking on the Gloss Angeles podcast with hosts Kirbie Johnson and Sara Tan, beauty entrepreneur Jerrod Blandino revealed for the first time that selling Too Faced was not part of his plans for the brand, and weighs in on what some in the industry describe as the ‘ELC curse’ Too Faced co-founder Jerrod Blandino has revealed what happened behind the scenes after the brand was acquired by Estée Lauder Companies (ELC), and weighed in on what some in the industry have branded the ‘ELC curse’ The beauty giant snapped up the make-up brand, which Blandino founded with Jeremy Johnson in 1998, for US$1.4bn in 2016, marking ELC’s biggest ever acquisition at the time.

articles.headline: Marketing Vanguard At Cannes: AI Is Moving From Fear To Confidence ft. Lara Balazs Of Adobe
articles.author: Jenny Rooney
articles.summary: The Marketing Vanguard Cannes series continues as host Jenny Rooney sits down with Lara Balazs, chief marketing officer and EVP of global marketing at Adobe. In this episode, Lara breaks down why enterprise AI adoption is shifting toward tangible workflow wins. She highlights how heavyweights like the NFL, Disney, and L’Oréal deploy Adobe Firefly to automate manual asset scaling while protecting proprietary IP. Learn why human empathy, brand trust, and strategic judgment remain irreplaceable in the age of generative AI.

articles.headline: All The Beauty Retail Expansions Of 2026
articles.author: Noor Lobad
articles.summary: Mexican body care brand Nopalera has entered 150 Costco stores with its Buena Vibra Shower Gel. The brand, founded in 2022 by Sandra Velasquez, also sells at Credo Beauty, Nordstrom and Kohl’s. Freaks of Nature, the sun and skin care brand cofounded by surfer Kelly Slater, is now at Credo. The lineup includes five products, priced from $20 for the Everyday Endurance Deodorant in two scents to $38 for the Peak Performance SPF 50.

articles.headline: Multifunctionality And Texture Reshape Simple Summer Beauty Routines
articles.author: William Nichols
articles.summary: Summer brings more opportunities for outdoor activities, but with the added outside time comes increased skin exposure to the elements. For summer beauty routines, industry experts point out that the season doesn’t test whether a skin care product works, rather if consumers keep using it once the heat sets in. Personal Care Insights sits down with Olay, Lubrizol, Beijing Gingko Group (BGG), and expert dermatologists, to discuss the latest innovations and summer cosmetic essentials, and how keeping skin care routines easy can aid consumers in their seasonal beauty journey.

articles.headline: Americans Fight Economic Gloom With Makeup And Movie Tickets
articles.author: Grace Thomas
articles.summary: Americans are carving out more room in their budgets for little luxuries as inflation and economic uncertainty push U.S. adults to postpone major purchases, new data shows, and a growing number say they feel financially insecure.

articles.headline: The “No-Makeup Makeup” Look Is On The Way Out, According To Reddit
articles.author: Marisa Meltzer
articles.summary: Reddit is best known as a forum for discussing how to retire in your thirties, trade conspiracy theories about medical school being a psyop, and gossip about which influencer is taking a GLP-1 but not admitting it. It is, in other words, not just a place for the extremely online to gather, but has earned a reputation for being a safe space for toxic thoughts to flourish.

articles.headline: The Beauty Industry's Fiercest Competitors Are Joining Forces. Here's Why.
articles.summary: At a time when TikTok content glamorizes tanning, and pushes sunscreen misinformation to your FYP, the #tanmaxxing trend has caught the attention of Gen Z, who are embracing sun habits that Dermatologists have long warned against. In response to these trends, ZO® Skin Health, the leading professional skincare brand, founded by Dr. Zein Obagi, has brought together a coalition of leading skincare brands to launch a first-of-its-kind social media campaign dedicated to one shared goal: making trusted skin health information that speaks to Gen Z. Joining ZO Skin Health in the campaign are leading brands Supergoop!, EltaMD, Black Girl Sunscreen, and Elizabeth Arden.

articles.headline: Researchers Call For Stronger Safety Testing Of Lip Cosmetics
articles.summary: New peer-reviewed publications find significant gaps in lip product regulation and safety testing, including reliance on inappropriate skin models and significant underestimation of usage and ingestion rates, leaving consumers exposed to potential risks. Two international critical reviews into the testing and legal framework for lip cosmetic products have identified significant blind spots when it comes to ingestion rate data, tissue testing types, and ingredients used in products. Lip cosmetics, including lipsticks, glosses, balms, oils, masks and stains, are classed as topical cosmetics for external use only. In practice, these products are routinely ingested and absorbed through lip tissue, resulting in a dual-pathway exposure route that existing frameworks were never designed to assess.

articles.headline: Chanel Sales Jump 16% In First Half
articles.summary: Chanel’s sales rose by double digits in the first half, beating luxury rivals including LVMH. This growth was boosted by the popular new collections from designer Matthieu Blazy. Bloomberg's Angelina Rascouet breaks down the latest figures.

articles.headline: Rahquel Purcell Named Chief Diversity, Equity And Inclusion Officer Of L’Oréal, North America
articles.author: Kaleigh Werner
articles.summary: L’Oréal has appointed a new chief diversity, equity and inclusion officer for its North America division. Rahquel Purcell will assume the role right away and report directly to Alexis Perakis-Valat, chief executive officer of L’Oréal USA and president of L’Oréal North America. The executive will keep her post on the leadership team of Margaret Johnston-Clarke, L’Oréal’s global diversity, equity and inclusion officer, as well as her seat on the management committee of L’Oréal USA.

articles.headline: Ulta Beauty In Yonkers Debuts New York's First Robot Manicure System
articles.author: John Meore
articles.summary: Yonkers is now home to New York’s first robotic manicure system, allowing customers to receive automated nail services in less than an hour.

articles.headline: Paper Packaging Sourcing: L’Oréal Makes Move With Canopy
articles.author: Ben Sillitoe
articles.summary: Beauty group L’Oréal has added its voice and industry leadership to the move towards more sustainable paper packaging by joining non-governmental organisation (NGO) Canopy’s Pack4Good programme. Pack4Good brings together brands committed to eliminating the risk of deforestation and forest degradation in their paper packaging, including impacts on ancient and endangered forests. Those signed up to the initiative are contributing to collective efforts to build supply chains that are more transparent, lower risk, and aligned with forest conservation.

articles.headline: New AI-Powered Clinical Software Can Fast-Forward Skin Research
articles.summary: An AI company focused on skin science has launched a research platform designed to make clinical skin studies faster to set up, easier to manage, and more practical to conduct on a much larger scale that has traditionally been possible. Instead of relying solely on traditional in-person studies that are expensive, time-consuming, and limited in size, Haut.AI’s Clinical Studies Software lets researchers run large-scale clinical studies in clinics, remotely from participants' homes, or a combination of both. “Our goal is not to replace clinical studies,” says Haut.AI’s CEO and co-founder, Anastasia Georgievskaya. “It's to enhance them by making skin measurable at scale.

articles.headline: The Human Moat: Beauty And Wellness Businesses Investors Believe Will Win The AI Revolution
articles.author: Rachel Brown
articles.summary: Some humans seem to have had it with artificial intelligence. From graduates booing AI mentions in commencement speeches to anxiety over job displacement and political opposition to data centers being built by AI companies, countercurrents are emerging alongside AI’s proliferation into practically every corner of life. Many beauty and wellness companies have embraced AI enthusiastically. L’Oréal recently announced a partnership with OpenAI to strengthen the company’s presence on ChatGPT and bring virtual makeup try-on to the platform. Sephora has launched an AI shopping assistant and integrated its services into ChatGPT, while Ulta Beauty has expanded its use of generative AI for personalization and product recommendations. Across the industry, companies are deploying AI for everything from formulation and trend forecasting to customer service and marketing.

articles.headline: ‘So Destructive’: Women Are Paying For Face Scans That Tell Them What Cosmetic Procedures To Get
articles.author: Laura O’Connor
articles.summary: Danielle, 37, didn’t always have issues with body image: she used to be a model and recalls receiving positive attention from men. However, when two years of unemployment plunged her into a period of financial insecurity, her confidence faded. “It was easy to wonder, if I was prettier, if some of my features were different, would that help?” she said. So, when Danielle saw videos on TikTok about a “facial analysis” service that claimed it could provide her with “science-backed” glow-up advice, she bought it without hesitation. Three-hundred and thirty dollars later, after sending in selfies to be analyzed, Danielle received her personalized 30-page report from the company Qoves.

articles.headline: Sephora And Olive Young Reveal Brand Lineup For Partnership
articles.author: Kathryn Hopkins
articles.summary: Many months in the making, Sephora and Olive Young are ready to show off their partnership. Launching Aug. 20, the joint venture brings 19 Olive Young-curated Korean beauty brands to 500 Sephora stores in the U.S. and sephora.com, with expansion planned across key global markets. The participating brands include Cell Fusion C, Rejuran, Thome, Wellage and Whipped, among others. Prices range from $4 to $69 for skin care and up to $299 for devices.

articles.headline: Black Beauty Brands Are Reclaiming The Block Party
articles.author: Bianca Lambert
articles.summary: My first experience with a block party was the Atlanta Black Arts Festival. My parents bought me my first piece of artwork, a hand-drawn black-and-white sketch of a Black ballerina, in 1992. It’s hanging on the wall in my home today. This event became a core memory for me. So much so that 34 years later, I can also remember the music ringing through Piedmont Park, the smell of food wafting in the air, and, of course, the overwhelming feeling of a community experience all those years ago. So to see the emergence over the last year of Black-founded beauty brands like The Black Beauty Club, Lab Beauty, Oui the People, and Sliq hosting block parties, it feels familiar and necessary at a time when many of us are craving one-to-one time with other people who look like us.

articles.headline: How Korean Beauty Made It To D-FW
articles.author: Katie Guenthner
articles.summary: The craze for Korean skincare hasn’t just arrived in Dallas, it’s been here. From spas to trending brands to specialized facials, Korean beauty is growing in the U.S. and in North Texas. Instagram and TikTok feeds fill users' screens with images of women with glassy, poreless and radiant skin — all using lotions and creams with ingredients from across the Pacific.

articles.headline: Reddit Releases The People’s Beauty Index
articles.author: Rachel Klemovitch
articles.summary: Reddit debuted its first-ever beauty report, distilling a year of authentic community conversations to reveal where beauty culture is headed next. Beauty is moving away from prescriptive, top-down trends toward a culture of participation. On Reddit, people are trading perfection for real, collaborative discovery and prioritizing participation over prescription to define beauty on their own terms.
